## [0.2.9] - 2026-10-14

### Security

- **The `critical` npm package is gone; the service now loads a page and its stylesheets with its own code and calls `penthouse-esm` (the Chrome-based extraction `critical` was built on) directly.** `npm audit` on 0.2.8's lockfile reported 11 findings (1 critical, 9 high, 1 moderate), seven of them one advisory in `braces` (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm, stack exhaustion on deeply nested patterns) that has no patched release and came in only through `critical`; on this release's lockfile it reports 0, and the lockfile shrinks from 408 to 125 entries. The replacement is four modules (`service/page-fetch.js`, `stylesheets.js`, `rebase.js`, `critical-css.js`), every request of which goes through the local policy proxy that already guarded Chrome, and which puts bounds on what a page or a server can cost (see "Changed"). For an ordinary page the critical CSS is the same: `service/fixtures/parity/` records 254 cases of what `critical@8.0.0` did, `npm test` replays them, and 53 further cases there are the deliberate differences. On the maintainer's own production site the CSS is byte-identical for both viewports with 11 requests instead of 64.
- **Chrome is pinned to 155.0.8059.39 (puppeteer 25.13.0 and its base image move with it).** Stable moved on from the 154.0.8037.92 pin (Stable since 2026-10-06, and the build the new base image ships). The pin, the base image and the `puppeteer` npm package are bumped together.
- **The published image carries the Debian fixes for `perl-base` and `libpng16-16`.** The weekly re-scan of the published 0.2.8 image failed its Trivy gate on 2026-10-12: `perl-base` 5.36.0-7+deb12u3 has CVE-2026-13221, CVE-2026-42496 and CVE-2026-8376 (CRITICAL) and ten more at HIGH/MEDIUM, all fixed in `5.36.0-7+deb12u4`, and `libpng16-16` has CVE-2026-46675, fixed in `1.6.39-2+deb12u6`. Both stay installed (`perl-base` is Essential, `libfreetype6` and `libcairo2` need `libpng16-16`), so both join the packages the Dockerfile upgrades in place, which are now ten. Until this release is published, the 0.2.8 image and `:latest` keep those findings.

### Changed

- **The service is stricter and bounded where `critical` quietly used whatever it got.** Everything an operator can notice is listed in [Upgrading from 0.2.8](https://github.com/solarssk/wp-critical-css/blob/v0.2.9/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md#upgrading-from-028): a page that answers with a non-2xx status, a non-HTML page, a redirect to a host other than `ALLOWED_HOSTNAME`, or a stylesheet on your own host that cannot be loaded now fails the job with a reason in the log (before, an error page was processed as the page and the sheet was dropped silently); a stylesheet on another host that cannot be loaded is skipped with one warning; fixed limits apply (page 10 MiB, one stylesheet 2 MiB, all stylesheets 8 MiB, 100 stylesheets, 5 redirects, 60 s to load everything). Nothing is retried inside a job, and the page and its stylesheets are fetched once per job (not once per viewport) with plain `GET` requests (no `HEAD` probes), which is why a page costs your site far fewer requests.
- **Requests for a page or a stylesheet carry a new User-Agent:** `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; wp-critical-css/<version>; +https://github.com/solarssk/wp-critical-css)`. Allow it if a firewall or bot filter in front of your site decides by User-Agent. The requests Chrome makes while rendering are unchanged.
- **The caps are not a memory guarantee.** A page inside them can still be more than the example compose file's 1 GiB container can lay out (more than about 2 MiB of CSS in all, or about 2 MiB of dense HTML); that limit sits in the rendering stage, which is the same code as in 0.2.8, and a bigger `mem_limit` moves it. See [Memory and very large pages](https://github.com/solarssk/wp-critical-css/blob/v0.2.9/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md#memory-and-very-large-pages).

### Deploy

- Container image: `ghcr.io/solarssk/wp-critical-css:0.2.9` (rolling `:latest`, `:0.2`), also published to `docker.io/solarssk/wp-critical-css:0.2.9`.
- WordPress plugin: `wp-critical-css-0.2.9.zip`, attached to this release. The plugin itself is unchanged; its version moves only to stay in lockstep with the service.
- No migration steps and no new setting. Before upgrading: allow the new User-Agent if a filter needs it, make sure `/tmp` is writable (the example compose file mounts a tmpfs there) and know how big your largest pages are. After upgrading, run a sweep ([section 6 of docs/DEPLOYMENT.md](https://github.com/solarssk/wp-critical-css/blob/v0.2.9/docs/DEPLOYMENT.md#6-backfill-existing-content)) and read `docker logs critical-css-service` for lines starting with `[critical-css] failed for` or `[critical-css] skipping`: they mark the pages that now behave differently.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/solarssk/wp-critical-css/blob/v0.2.9/CHANGELOG.md)
